title: Stories the Qur'an Tells
bigQuestion: What stories does the Qur'an tell, and which ones do other families know too?

story.title: The Ant Who Warned Her Friends
story.kicker: A tiny ant sees a king's army coming and calls out to all the other ants.
paragraphs: The Qur'an tells a story about a king named Sulayman. In English, his name is Solomon. Muslims believe he was a prophet. A prophet brings a message from God. The Qur'an says Sulayman could understand birds and other animals.
One day, Sulayman marched with his army. There were people, and there were jinn, and there were birds. The ground shook with their steps. They came to a valley where many ants lived.
A tiny ant looked up. She saw the army coming closer. She called out to all the other ants. "Go into your homes! Hurry! Sulayman and his army are coming. They might step on you and not even know it."
Sulayman heard the ant. The Qur'an says he smiled. He thanked God for letting him understand her words. And the ants hurried home, safe. This story is in a surah called The Ant.
story.think: The ant was tiny, but she helped her friends. What did she do that was brave or kind?

lessons.title: Nuh and the Big Boat
lessons.mainIdea: The Qur'an tells about Nuh (Noah), who built a big boat and was saved from a flood.
reading: The Qur'an tells a story about *Nuh*. In English, his name is Noah. Muslims believe Nuh was a *prophet*, a person who brings a message from God. He told people to worship one God.
The Qur'an says most people did not listen. So God told Nuh to build a big boat, an ark. Then rain came, and water rose. Nuh, his family and the animals were safe on the boat.
The Bible tells a story about Noah too. The two books tell it in different ways. But many families know a story about Noah and a boat. Muslim, Jewish and Christian families all do.

words.d: the Arabic name for Noah; the Qur'an says he built a big boat
a person who brings a message from God, as Muslims believe

look.title: The Water Goes Down
look.text: The Qur'an says that after the flood, the earth was told to swallow its water. The sky was told to stop raining. The water went down, and the boat came to rest on a mountain.
look.cite: Qur'an 11:44, Surah Hud, paraphrased in simple words from Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran, 1930
look.prompt: Where did the boat stop when the water went down?

check.q: What is the English name for Nuh?
check.why: Nuh is the Arabic name for Noah. Yunus is Jonah and Musa is Moses.

check.q: What did Nuh build, as the Qur'an tells it?
check.why: The Qur'an says God told Nuh to build an ark, a big boat, before the flood.

check.q: Which other book tells a story about Noah and a boat?
check.why: The Bible also tells about Noah and the ark. The two books tell it in different ways.

lessons.title: Yunus and the Big Fish
lessons.mainIdea: The Qur'an tells about Yunus (Jonah), who was swallowed by a big fish and then set safe on land.
reading: The Qur'an tells about *Yunus*. In English, his name is Jonah. The Qur'an says Yunus left his people and got on a ship. Then he was thrown into the sea.
A big fish swallowed him. Inside the dark fish, Yunus called out to God. He said he was sorry. The Qur'an says God heard him, and the fish put him on the shore.
There is a surah named Yunus. The Bible tells about Jonah and a big fish too. Many children know this story from home. Some know it from a book or a song.

words.d: the Arabic name for Jonah; the Qur'an says a big fish swallowed him
the land at the edge of the sea

look.title: Inside the Dark Fish
look.text: Look at Yunus inside the fish. It is dark. It is quiet. He cannot see the sky or the sea. He is all alone. He closes his eyes and calls out to God. Then, the Qur'an says, the fish sets him on the shore, and a plant grows to give him shade.
look.prompt: What did Yunus do when he was in the dark? What happened next?

check.q: What swallowed Yunus, as the Qur'an tells it?
check.why: The Qur'an says a big fish swallowed Yunus. The Bible says a great fish swallowed Jonah.

check.q: What did Yunus do inside the fish?
choices: He sang a song about ants
check.why: The Qur'an says Yunus called out to God in the dark and said he was sorry (21:87).

check.q: What is the English name for Yunus?
check.why: Yunus is the Arabic name for Jonah. Nuh is Noah and Yusuf is Joseph.

lessons.title: Musa in the River
lessons.mainIdea: The Qur'an says Musa's (Moses's) mother put him in a basket on the river, and he was found and kept safe.
reading: The Qur'an tells about *Musa*. In English, his name is Moses. When Musa was a baby, a king called *Pharaoh* was hurting the baby boys of Musa's people.
The Qur'an says Musa's mother put him in a basket on the river. Pharaoh's wife found him. She loved him and kept him. Musa's sister watched and helped bring him back to his mother to be fed.
Musa is named more times in the Qur'an than any other prophet. The Bible tells the basket story too. Many families know the baby in the basket.

words.d: the Arabic name for Moses; the prophet named most often in the Qur'an
the king of Egypt in the story of Musa

look.title: A Mother's Promise
look.text: The Qur'an says God told Musa's mother to feed her baby, and if she was afraid, to put him in the river and not to fear. She was told that her baby would come back to her.
look.cite: Qur'an 28:7, Surah Al-Qasas (The Story), paraphrased in simple words from Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran, 1930
look.prompt: Musa's mother was afraid. What was she told would happen to her baby?

check.q: Where did Musa's mother put him, as the Qur'an tells it?
choices: In a basket on the river
check.why: The Qur'an says Musa's mother put him in the river, and Pharaoh's wife found him (28:7-9).

check.q: Who found baby Musa?
check.why: The Qur'an says Pharaoh's wife found the baby and wanted to keep him.

check.q: Which prophet is named most often in the Qur'an?
check.why: Musa (Moses) is named more times in the Qur'an than any other prophet.

lessons.title: Musa at the Sea
lessons.mainIdea: The Qur'an says the sea opened for Musa and his people, and they walked across to safety.
reading: Musa grew up. Muslims believe God sent him as a prophet. The Qur'an says Musa told *Pharaoh* to let his people go free. Pharaoh said no.
Musa led his people away. Pharaoh's army chased them. They came to the sea. The Qur'an says God told Musa to strike the sea with his stick. The water split, and each side stood up like a mountain.
Musa's people walked across on dry ground. They were safe. The Bible tells about the sea opening too. It is one of the most famous stories in both books.

words.d: the king who would not let Musa's people go free
to break or open into parts

look.title: Walls of Water
look.text: Look at Musa's people at the edge of the sea. Behind them, the army is coming. In front of them, the water is wide. Musa strikes the water with his stick. The Qur'an says the sea splits open. Water stands up on the left like a mountain. Water stands up on the right like a mountain. A dry path runs between them.
look.prompt: Which way should the people walk now? How do you think they felt?

check.q: What did Musa do at the sea, as the Qur'an tells it?
choices: He struck the sea with his stick
check.why: The Qur'an (26:63) says God told Musa to strike the sea with his stick, and it split.

check.q: What did each side of the water look like?
check.why: The Qur'an says each part of the water stood up like a great mountain.

check.q: Who was chasing Musa's people?
check.why: Pharaoh's army chased Musa's people to the sea. Sulayman's army is in the story of the ant.

lessons.title: Ibrahim and Ismail Build the Kaaba
lessons.mainIdea: The Qur'an says Ibrahim (Abraham) and his son Ismail built the Kaaba, the square building in Mecca.
reading: The Qur'an tells about *Ibrahim*. In English, his name is Abraham. Muslims believe he was a prophet who worshiped one God. Jews and Christians tell about Abraham too.
The Qur'an says Ibrahim and his son *Ismail* built the *Kaaba*. The Kaaba is a square building in Mecca. As they built, they prayed. They asked God to accept their work.
Today Muslims face the Kaaba when they pray. Many travel to Mecca to see it. When they do, many think of Ibrahim and Ismail.

words.d: the Arabic name for Abraham; the Qur'an says he built the Kaaba with his son
the Arabic name for Ishmael, Ibrahim's son
the square building in Mecca that Muslims face when they pray

look.title: Raising the Walls
look.text: The Qur'an says that Ibrahim and Ismail raised the foundations of the House, the Kaaba. As they worked, they prayed, "Our Lord, accept this from us."
look.cite: Qur'an 2:127, Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow), paraphrased in simple words from Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran, 1930
look.prompt: Who built the Kaaba, as the Qur'an tells it? What did they say while they built?

check.q: What is the English name for Ibrahim?
check.why: Ibrahim is the Arabic name for Abraham. Jews and Christians tell about Abraham too.

check.q: What did Ibrahim and Ismail build, as the Qur'an tells it?
check.why: The Qur'an (2:127) says Ibrahim and Ismail raised the walls of the Kaaba in Mecca.

check.q: What do Muslims do with the Kaaba today?
choices: They face it when they pray
They sail it on the sea
check.why: Muslims all over the world face the Kaaba when they pray. Many travel to Mecca to see it.

lessons.title: Maryam and Baby Isa
lessons.mainIdea: The Qur'an tells about Maryam (Mary) and her baby Isa (Jesus), and a whole surah is named for Maryam.
reading: The Qur'an tells about *Maryam*. In English, her name is Mary. One whole surah has her name. Muslims believe an angel told her she would have a baby boy.
The Qur'an says her baby was *Isa*. In English, his name is Jesus. The Qur'an says Maryam rested under a palm tree. Fresh dates fell for her to eat.
Muslims believe Isa was a prophet. They believe he healed people and taught them. Christians tell about Mary and Jesus too. They believe some different things about him. Both books honor Maryam.

words.d: the Arabic name for Mary; a surah of the Qur'an is named for her
the Arabic name for Jesus; Muslims believe he was a prophet

look.title: Under the Palm Tree
look.text: Look at Maryam sitting under a tall palm tree. She is tired and alone. The Qur'an says a voice told her not to be sad. It told her to shake the tree, and ripe dates fell down for her. A little stream ran by her feet.
look.prompt: What did Maryam get from the tree and the stream? Why do you think the Qur'an tells this part?

check.q: What is the English name for Maryam?
check.why: Maryam is the Arabic name for Mary. A surah of the Qur'an is named for her.

check.q: Who is Isa, as Muslims believe?
choices: A prophet, the son of Maryam
check.why: Muslims believe Isa (Jesus) was a prophet, born to Maryam. Christians believe some different things about him.

check.q: What fell from the palm tree for Maryam, as the Qur'an tells it?
check.why: The Qur'an (19:25) says ripe dates fell from the palm tree for Maryam.

sections.title: The Ant and Stories We Share

lessons.title: Sulayman and the Ant
lessons.mainIdea: The Qur'an says an ant warned the other ants about Sulayman's (Solomon's) army, and Sulayman smiled at her words.
reading: You read the story of the ant at the start of this chapter. The king was *Sulayman*. In English, his name is Solomon. The Qur'an says he understood the speech of birds and animals.
The ant told her friends to hurry into their homes. Sulayman heard her and *smiled*. Then he thanked God. The Qur'an says he asked to be a person who does good.
This story is in the surah called The Ant, surah 27. The Bible tells about King Solomon too, but not about the ant. That part is in the Qur'an.

words.d: the Arabic name for Solomon; the Qur'an says he understood the speech of animals
made a happy face; Sulayman smiled at the ant's words

look.title: What the Ant Said
look.text: The Qur'an says an ant called out, "Ants, go into your homes, so that Sulayman and his army do not crush you without knowing it." Sulayman smiled at her words and thanked God.
look.cite: Qur'an 27:18-19, Surah An-Naml (The Ant), paraphrased in simple words from Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran, 1930
look.prompt: The ant says the army would not know it stepped on the ants. Why does that matter in her warning?

check.q: What is the English name for Sulayman?
check.why: Sulayman is the Arabic name for Solomon. The Qur'an says he was a king and a prophet.

check.q: What did Sulayman do when he heard the ant?
check.why: The Qur'an (27:19) says Sulayman smiled at the ant's words and thanked God.

check.q: Which surah tells the story of the ant?
check.why: The story of the ant is in surah 27, which is named The Ant (An-Naml).

lessons.title: Stories Many Families Share
lessons.mainIdea: Many stories in the Qur'an are about people the Bible tells about too, so many families share them.
reading: The Qur'an tells about Nuh, Yunus, Musa and Maryam. The *Bible* tells about Noah, Jonah, Moses and Mary. These are the same people. They have different names in each book.
The two books do not tell the stories the same way. Some parts are alike. Some parts are different. Muslims, Jews and Christians each read their own book.
Some surahs are named for these people. When you hear a story about a boat, a big fish or a basket, you can say, "The Qur'an tells that story. The Bible tells it too."

words.d: the holy book of Christians; Jews share its first part, the Hebrew Bible

look.title: Surahs Named for People in Stories
look.cite: The Qur'an, surah names and numbers in the standard order of the 114 surahs
look.prompt: Which of these surahs comes first in the Qur'an? Which comes last?

check.q: Which two books tell stories about Noah, Moses and Mary?
check.why: The Qur'an and the Bible both tell about these people. They use different names and tell the stories in different ways.

check.q: Musa is the Arabic name for which person in the Bible?
check.why: Musa is Moses. Nuh is Noah and Sulayman is Solomon.

check.q: Do the Qur'an and the Bible tell the stories in the same way?
choices: No, some parts are alike and some are different
Yes, every word is the same
No, the Bible has no stories
check.why: The two books share people and stories, but they tell them differently. Each faith reads its own book.

review.q: Who built a big boat, as the Qur'an tells it?
review.why: The Qur'an says Nuh (Noah) built the ark before the flood.
The Qur'an says a big fish swallowed Yunus (Jonah), and then he was set on the shore.

choices: In a basket on the river
review.why: The Qur'an says Musa's mother put him in the river, and Pharaoh's wife found him.

review.q: Who built the Kaaba with his son Ismail, as the Qur'an tells it?
review.why: The Qur'an (2:127) says Ibrahim (Abraham) and Ismail raised the walls of the Kaaba.

review.q: A whole surah is named for which woman?
review.why: Surah 19 is named Maryam (Mary). It tells about her and her baby Isa.

review.q: Who smiled at the words of a tiny ant?
review.why: The Qur'an (27:19) says Sulayman (Solomon) smiled when he heard the ant warn her friends.
